title: SYSK Selects: How The Hum Works
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the December 2014 episode "How the Hum Works." Josh introduces it as a favorite pick. The hosts explain the Hum, a low-frequency drone heard by a small percentage of people (mostly in Western, English-speaking countries and rural areas), which many describe as coming from an external source. They cover the World Hum Map and Database run by Glenn McPherson, Dr. Colin Novak's Windsor Hum investigation traced to Zug Island steel plant, the Taos Hum investigation, theories involving US military VLF/ELF transmissions (HAARP, TACAMO), the tinnitus and mass-delusion explanations (David Deming), habituation and sensitization, claims linking the Hum to violent acts (Sandy Hook, Navy Yard shooting), and the Portuguese Air Force workshop study of low-frequency noise and vibroacoustic disease. The episode closes with listener mail about a limousine cattle ranch in South Dakota.

segments.title: Rerun intro and vocal fry banter
segments.summary: Josh introduces this SYSK Selects pick from December 2014 and the hosts open with banter about the hum sound and vocal fry.

segments.title: What the Hum is and where it's heard
segments.summary: The hosts define the Hum as a low-frequency drone heard by about two percent of people in certain places, often at night and indoors and in rural areas, and often named after their locations such as the Taos Hum and Bristol Hum. Sufferers say others cannot hear it and it can disrupt sleep.

segments.title: World Hum Map and geographic pattern
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Glenn McPherson's World Hum Map and Database, which shows reports concentrated in the US, Great Britain, Western Europe, Canada and South Africa, and credit Jared Keller's Mic article.

segments.title: Tinnitus, mass delusion and David Deming's study
segments.summary: The hosts describe the medical explanations for the Hum, including tinnitus and mass delusion, and David Deming's 2004 study that considered them and other explanations.

segments.title: ELF/VLF radio, HAARP and TACAMO theories
segments.summary: The hosts explain extremely low and very low frequency radio waves and theories linking the Hum to US military transmissions, including HAARP in Alaska and the TACAMO submarine communication system, and note the debate over whether the Hum is electromagnetic or acoustic.

segments.title: Windsor, Taos and official investigations
segments.summary: Dr. Colin Novak's year-long study of the Windsor Hum traced it to a steel plant on Zug Island in Michigan, and the Taos Hum prompted an investigation by the University of New Mexico and Sandia Labs, which could not identify a cause. The X-Files episode Drive is also mentioned.

segments.title: Age, habituation and sensitization
segments.summary: The hosts discuss why older people may hear low frequencies better, the difference between habituation and sensitization, and how these may relate to Hum sufferers.

segments.title: Hum linked to violence: Sandy Hook and Navy Yard
segments.summary: The hosts describe Steve Collaz's claim that a nearby gas pipeline hum may have contributed to Adam Lanza's actions at Sandy Hook, and Aaron Alexis's note about ELF attacks before the Navy Yard shooting. They note skeptics' views and the role of conspiracy communities.

segments.title: Portugal aircraft workshop and vibroacoustic disease
segments.summary: The hosts describe the late 1970s Portuguese Air Force workshop (OGMA) where Castello Branco noticed epilepsy-like seizures and ten workers were diagnosed with late-onset epilepsy, and the autopsy of Philippe Pedro, which the hosts link to low-frequency noise damage and vibroacoustic disease.

segments.title: Further reading and related podcasts
segments.summary: The hosts recommend reading Jared Keller's article and David Deming's paper, and mention related sites and podcasts such as Radiolab-style science shows, Roman Mars's 99% Invisible, and Damn Interesting.

segments.title: Listener mail: limousine ranch
segments.summary: Jennifer Coleman writes about her plumber husband being sent to Anderson's Limousin Ranch in rural South Dakota, and the hosts joke about limousine cattle and a Kevin Costner trailer.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts ask listeners to send in mail and direct them to the website and social accounts.
